items.title: mltreelib
items.text:
Tree-based machine learning with a Rust core. A data & feature layer that treats missing data as first-class, an adjustable benchmark generator with known ground truth, and a tree learner that handles categoricals and missing values natively — with rpart-faithful printing, SVG diagrams, and LightGBM-style monotone & interaction constraints.

  • Rust core (mltreelib-core), thin Python shell (PyO3)
  • Scikit-learn-shaped API — without the scikit-learn dependency
  • NA and NaN handled end-to-end: missing in → missing out; imputation opt-in
  • 51 TabArena-v0.1 benchmark datasets on board, plus a generator whose knobs control how much signal lives in group and hierarchy structure
uv sync                                          # venv + Rust extension (maturin)
uv run python examples/quickstart.py             # fit, print, visualize
uv run python examples/churn_demo.py             # end-to-end on real data
I want to… go to install it Installation see it work in 30 seconds Quickstart solve a real problem Examples — end-to-end walkthrough wrangle data & encodings Examples — Data Processing know every knob Examples — Model building & predictions read the numbers Examples — Inspection draw the tree Examples — Visualization see how it compares Benchmarks — ELO look up every parameter API reference

Try it right now

uv run python examples/quickstart.py fits a tree, prints it in rpart format and writes an SVG diagram. The end-to-end walkthrough then does the same on 10,000 real bank customers.

The research program, roadmap and contribution rules live in the repository (README.md, AGENTS.md).

items.title: What our side of the page looks like
items.text:
from mltreelib import ModelTree            # that is the install story
m = ModelTree(leaf="linear")               # or leaf="mean", leaf_cols="path"
m.fit(x, y)                                # x may contain None — NAs first-class
m.predict(x)                               # never fails on a missing value
m.leaves()[0]                              # coef, na_coef, mean, std, quantiles
m.profile()                                # per-level timings built in
  • one dependency family (Rust core + thin Python shell);
  • NAs are first-class (learned split directions, NA-indicator leaf terms);
  • every leaf keeps its statistics and a t-digest;
  • the tree reproduces rpart exactly when configured as CART (mean leaves), so results are checkable against the reference implementations.

items.title: How the Elo works (our protocol)
items.text:
Elo comes from chess: every model carries a rating; when two models "play", the winner takes points from the loser proportionally to how surprising the result was.

  • Expected score of A against B: E_A = 1 / (1 + 10^((R_B - R_A) / 400)) (equal ratings → 50%; a 200-point underdog still expects ~24%).
  • After a game with actual score S_A (1 win, 0.5 draw, 0 loss): R_A += K * (S_A - E_A), R_B += K * (S_B - E_B), with K = 32 here.

What counts as a game: on each dataset, every unordered pair of models plays once — lower RMSE wins (equal RMSE = draw). So 16 datasets × n·(n-1)/2 games per full field. The order is deterministic (datasets sorted, pairs lexicographic), so the whole board is reproducible from the score file.

How to read it:

  • Ratings are relative — the zero point moves when models enter or leave (the same tree scored 901 with 13 models and 858 with 18). Watch the ordering and the gaps, not the absolute numbers.
  • One model with several flavors (our three leaf kinds) splits its own wins — treat them as separate competitors, which is intended.
  • K = 32 keeps the board responsive to real differences; over 5 datasets a genuinely better model climbs fast.
  • TabArena's numbers are not comparable — different protocol (their own tournament + bootstrapping on 51 datasets incl. classification). They are a scale anchor only.

Reproduce: elo_prepare.py (data, once) → elo_score_r.R → elo_score_python.py → elo_score_rust.py (each environment, incremental upsert) → elo_report.py (this Elo computation).

items.title: Why this page exists
items.text: Benchmarks should be about models, not plumbing. The Elo arena (examples/elo_prepare.py → elo_score_r.R / elo_score_python.py / elo_score_rust.py → elo_report.py, one scores file) exists so the field can be re-run incrementally — but assembling it highlighted how much incidental complexity the alternatives impose. That complexity is our documentation.

items.title: Installation
items.text: mltreelib is a Python package with a Rust core — one wheel, no transitive dependencies.

items.title: From PyPI
items.text: pip install mltreelib

items.title: With uv
items.text: uv add mltreelib

items.title: From source
items.text:
Building from source needs a Rust toolchain (rustup) and maturin:

git clone https://github.com/jkapila/mltreelib
cd mltreelib
uv run maturin develop        # builds the Rust core into your environment

items.title: Verify the install
items.text:
uv run python -c "from mltreelib import ModelTree; print(ModelTree())"

An unfitted tree refuses to print its structure (by design); the call should raise ValueError: ModelTree is not fitted. Fit anything and print(model) shows the rpart-style tree.

items.title: Plotting (optional extra)
items.text:
Charts and diagrams ride on the standard rendering wheels — install them only when you build figures:

pip install mltreelib[plotting]     # matplotlib + pygraphviz + seaborn
# or
uv sync --extra plotting

mltreelib.plots (metric charts) and ModelTree.to_dot() + pygraphviz (tree diagrams) are the two consumers. The core library never imports them.

items.title: What you get
items.text:
ModelTree the tree: fit / predict, rpart-style text, SVG diagram, constraints 18 encoders OneHot, Hashing, Target, CatBoost, WoE, James-Stein, Count, Leave-One-Out, M-Estimator, Base-N, Sum, Quantile, TF-IDF, Embedding, … scalers & builders VariableScaler, GroupedScaler, DatasetBuilder, IndexMapper Metrics regression / classification / regression-by-group reports dataset helpers list_datasets, load_dataset, summarize, generate, calendar / lag / window transforms

Numerics run in the Rust core; the data layer is the same code the benchmarks run on.

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
Fit a tree, read it, see it. The full script lives at examples/quickstart.py.

from mltreelib import ModelTree, Metrics

# Toy data: a step function plus a linear trend (deterministic).
x = [[float(i % 8)] for i in range(80)]
y = [2.0 * (i % 8) + (5.0 if i % 8 > 4 else 0.0) + ((i * 13) % 7) * 0.05 for i in range(80)]

# Defaults are already tuned (regularized linear leaves, shallow depth).
model = ModelTree()
model.fit(x, y)

pred = model.predict([[float(v)] for v in range(8)])
print("predictions:", [round(p, 2) for p in pred])
print("metrics:", {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in
                   Metrics().regression(y_test, pred).items() if k in ("rmse", "mae", "r2")})

print(model)                                  # rpart-style tree text
dot = model.to_dot()                         # graphviz does the layout
pgv.AGraph(string=dot).draw("docs/assets/quickstart_tree.svg", prog="dot")

Three things to notice:

  • The tree prints like rpart — same numbering, indentation, deviance and yval columns, * on leaves. If you know rpart, you already know how to read this.
  • to_dot() describes the tree, graphviz draws it — one box per node with the split condition, n, and fitted value; edges labeled with thresholds. Layout belongs to graphviz (via pygraphviz); we don't reinvent it.
  • Defaults are tuned — leaf="linear" with a small ridge (l2) penalty at shallow depth is the configuration that won our benchmark bake-off.

items.title: Issue tracker: Local Markdown
items.text: Issues and specs for this repo live as markdown files in .scratch/.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
• One feature per directory: .scratch/<feature-slug>/
  • The spec is .scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md
  • Implementation issues are one file per ticket at .scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md, numbered from 01, never a single combined tickets file
  • Triage state is recorded as a Status: line near the top of each issue file (see triage-labels.md for the role strings)
  • Comments and conversation history append to the bottom of the file under a ## Comments heading

items.title: When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"
items.text: Create a new file under .scratch/<feature-slug>/ (creating the directory if needed).

items.title: When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"
items.text: Read the file at the referenced path. The user will normally pass the path or the issue number directly.

items.title: Wayfinding operations
items.text:
Used by /wayfinder. The map is a file with one child file per ticket.

  • Map: .scratch/<effort>/map.md (the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body).
  • Child ticket: .scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md, numbered from 01, with the question in the body. A Type: line records the ticket type (research/prototype/grilling/task); a Status: line records claimed/resolved.
  • Blocking: a Blocked by: NN, NN line near the top. A ticket is unblocked when every file it lists is resolved.
  • Frontier: scan .scratch/<effort>/issues/ for files that are open, unblocked, and unclaimed; first by number wins.
  • Claim: set Status: claimed and save before any work.
  • Resolve: append the answer under an ## Answer heading, set Status: resolved, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far in map.md.

items.title: Benchmark datasets
items.text:
datasets/ holds the full TabArena-v0.1 suite: 51 curated tabular datasets (87.4 MB, OpenML suite 457) — 7 regression, 44 classification, 4 small (<1k rows), 40 medium, 7 large (up to 150k rows), including high-cardinality categorical sets. Files are parquet with categoricals preserved as strings; datasets/MANIFEST.md lists per-dataset target, size, license and source.

from mltreelib import list_datasets, load_dataset

list_datasets()                 # ['APSFailure', 'Bank_Customer_Churn', ...]
ds = load_dataset("churn")
ds["n_rows"], ds["n_cols"]      # 5000, 20
ds["dtypes"]                    # {"state": "categorical", "account_length": "numeric", ...}
ds["na_counts"]                 # missing shown by default

load_dataset returns the same shape as DatasetBuilder.build(), so it feeds straight back into the data layer.

BeyondArena

The beyond-IID extension (temporal/grouped splits) ships via the separate data-foundry package and is intentionally not vendored; see the manifest for notes.

items.title: ELO
items.text: One scoreboard, one protocol, every model scored on the same prepared data.

items.title: The protocol
items.text:
• Data: the regression sets below, one 80/20 split (seed 7), identical numeric encodings for every scorer (prepared once by examples/elo_prepare.py — no per-model preprocessing luck).
  • Matchups: per dataset, every unordered pair of models "plays" once; the lower test RMSE wins (tie = draw).
  • Ratings: standard Elo, K=32, everyone starts at 1000, deterministic round-robin order. Ratings are field-relative — adding models moves numbers around, so compare within one run.

Reproduce: uv run python examples/elo_report.py (reads benchmarks/elo_scores.csv, written incrementally by the R, Python and Rust scorers).

items.title: Development rounds (ours vs the frozen field)
items.text:
The external field (R packages, LightGBM, CatBoost, CTBoost, forust, perpetual, MARS, sklearn, modeltrees) is scored once and frozen in benchmarks/elo_baselines.csv — where we started. Every development round re-scores only the ModelTree variants on the same prepared splits:

uv run python examples/elo_round.py                 # all datasets
ELO_DATASETS=abalone,boston uv run python examples/elo_round.py   # a subset
uv run python examples/elo_round.py --freeze        # deliberately re-anchor

Each round prints started (frozen baseline) -> reached Elo for every ModelTree flavor, with per-fit timings in the scores file — so progress across iterations is visible instead of silently overwritten. The full from-scratch rebuild (all models, groups of 5 datasets, shareable intermediate state after each group) is bash examples/elo_run_groups.sh.

The field's raw scores (per dataset RMSE/MAE/fit time) live in benchmarks/elo_scores.csv; the longer research log is in docs/field-notes.md.

items.title: Running a round (repeatable, with provenance)
items.text:
One command re-scores our four flavors against the frozen field:

uv run python examples/elo_round.py                    # all 18 datasets
ELO_DATASETS=abalone,boston uv run python examples/elo_round.py   # subset

Every round records what created its numbers:

  • benchmarks/rounds/<stamp>/settings.json — the exact settings dict each flavor was fit with (single-sourced: the manifest records the same dict variants() builds from, so record and reality cannot drift), the git SHA, the dataset list, every result row, and Elo before → after.
  • benchmarks/elo_round.log — stdlib logging output (file + console), one line per round: timestamp, stamp, sha, dataset count, per-model Elo before->after. This is the first place to look for "what did we change and what did it move".
  • benchmarks/elo_scores.csv — the live board (our rows upserted); benchmarks/elo_baselines.csv — the frozen anchor ("where we started").

Tuned settings from examples/hpo_optuna.py print in the same dict shape — paste them into SETTINGS in elo_round.py to score a tuned flavor.

items.title: Hyperparameter search (Optuna)
items.text:
The full ModelTree growth surface is a search space — and Optuna is the wheel we borrow for it. examples/hpo_optuna.py tunes depth, leaf size, ridge, leaf kind, criterion, the split grid, categorical search, the imbalance knobs and pruning on a seeded TPE study:

uv run --with pandas --with optuna python examples/hpo_optuna.py 40

The objective is plain — fit, score, return RMSE. Every suggestion maps 1:1 to a ModelTree keyword:

params = dict(
    max_depth=trial.suggest_int("max_depth", 1, 8),
    min_rows=trial.suggest_int("min_rows", 5, 200, log=True),
    l2=trial.suggest_float("l2", 1e-3, 10.0, log=True),
    leaf=trial.suggest_categorical("leaf", ["linear", "mean"]),
    leaf_cols=trial.suggest_categorical("leaf_cols", ["all", "path"]),
    gain=trial.suggest_categorical("gain", ["sse", "sdr"]),
    split_precision=trial.suggest_categorical("split_precision", [None, 0.1, 0.01]),
    cat_search=trial.suggest_categorical("cat_search", ["cumulative", "single_vs_rest", "both"]),
    alpha=trial.suggest_float("alpha", 0.0, 0.2),
    imbalance_penalty=trial.suggest_float("imbalance_penalty", 1e-3, 100.0, log=True),
    prune=trial.suggest_categorical("prune", ["none", "bic", "mdl"]),
)
m = ModelTree(**params)
m.fit(xtr, ytr, dtypes=dtypes)
return Metrics().regression(yte, m.predict(xte))["rmse"]

items.title: Growth knobs — max_depth, min_rows, min_gain
items.text: Deeper is not better: depth 12 chases noise (598.6 vs 577.0), and coarser leaves win outright (555.6 with min_rows=500) — on 54k rows the tree prefers fewer, steadier leaves. min_gain is the numerical noise floor.

items.title: Leaf models — and why the default keeps ridge
items.text:
leaf="mean" fits piecewise constants (884.5); leaf="linear" fits piecewise slopes and wins here (577.0). leaf_cols="path" restricts leaf regressions to the columns used on the path — fewer coefficients, less variance, more bias (1137.5).

Then the important one: l1=0, l2=0 explodes (r² = −40499). Pure-OLS leaves on raw, collinear scales produce wild coefficients and nine-million-dollar predictions. The small default ridge is not cosmetic — it is load-bearing, and it is closed-form (fast). This is exactly why regularization earns its own upcoming example.

items.title: Row weights
items.text: fit(x, y, w) — upweighting small stones (2x carat<1) shifts the fitted leaf values toward the weighted rows without touching the structure.

items.title: Winnowing — min_relevance / winnow()
items.text:
res = winnow(xtr, ytr, min_relevance=0.05)   # {"kept": [...], "relevance": [...]}

Univariate relevance screening drops 11 of 26 columns (mostly one-hot levels) before the split search; the winnowed fit keeps its accuracy on half the columns (898.1). Same screen runs inside fit when min_relevance is set.

items.title: Monotone constraints
items.text: A domain fact: price never falls as carat rises. monotone=[…, +1, …] enforces it at split choice and in leaf coefficients — costing almost nothing here (601.8 vs 577.0) because the fact is true.

items.title: Interaction groups
items.text: interaction_groups=[[carat…], [rest…]] — every root-to-leaf path may split only one group (LightGBM-style interaction constraints). Small cost (583.7), bounded interaction structure.

items.title: End-to-end walkthrough — churn
items.text:
The whole story on one real problem: predict who leaves the bank. Typed ingest throughout — country and gender enter the tree as levels (a distinct value is a level; the split search partitions level sets), NAs route as-is, and nothing is ever encoded for the tree. Strings are coded once by IndexMapper because the fit takes numbers — that mapping is a pipeline step, not a tree step. The tree is a regressor; fit on a 0/1 churn target it is a solid, fully interpretable baseline (threshold at 0.5).

Script: examples/churn_demo.py (uv run --with pandas --with pyarrow --with matplotlib python examples/churn_demo.py).

from mltreelib import IndexMapper, Metrics, ModelTree

y = (df["churn"] == "Yes").astype(float).tolist()

cols = [c for c in df.columns if c != "churn"]
mappers = {}
for col in ("country", "gender"):
    m = IndexMapper()
    m.fit(col, [None if pd.isna(v) else str(v) for v in df[col]])
    mappers[col] = m

dtypes, columns = [], []
for col in cols:
    raw = [None if pd.isna(v) else v for v in df[col]]
    if col in mappers:
        dtypes.append("categorical")
        columns.append(mappers[col].transform(col, [None if v is None else str(v) for v in raw]))
    else:
        dtypes.append("numeric")
        columns.append([None if v is None else float(v) for v in raw])
X = [list(row) for row in zip(*columns)]

model = ModelTree(max_depth=4, min_rows=40)
model.fit(xtr, ytr, dtypes=dtypes)

items.title: API reference — Data
items.text: The data & feature layer: everything that turns raw columns into numeric matrices. All names come from import mltreelib.

items.title: Dataset helpers
items.text:
• list_datasets() — the bundled benchmark sets (see DataSets).
  • load_dataset(name) — load one as a frame.
  • summarize(df) — per-column summary including n_missing by default.

items.title: Winnowing (column screening)
items.text: • winnow(x, y, min_relevance=0.05) → {"kept": [column indices], "relevance": [score per column]} — screen columns by univariate relevance against the target before training (the cheap pre-split screening LightGBM calls feature pre-filtering). The same screen runs inside ModelTree.fit when min_relevance is set.

items.title: Categorical encoders
items.text:
All follow fit(values) → transform(values) with None passed through as missing; unseen levels map to missing.

encoder shape OneHotEncoder levels(), transform → {level: [0/1 column]} (missing → all-zero row) HashingEncoder(n_buckets) fixed-width hashing TargetEncoder(smoothing) smoothed target mean; prior() CatBoostEncoder(prior, permutations, seed) ordered target statistics WoEEncoder(prior) weight of evidence JamesSteinEncoder shrinkage estimator CountEncoder frequency encoding LeaveOneOutEncoder leave-one-out target mean MEstimatorEncoder(smoothing) m-estimate smoothing BaseNEncoder base-N numeric code SumEncoder sum (effect) coding QuantileEncoder quantile target statistics TfidfEncoder tf-idf over categories EmbeddingEncoder(dim, lr, epochs, seed, task) learned embeddings (Rust core)

items.title: Scalers & builders
items.text:
• VariableScaler(normalize) — per-column numeric scaling with invertible inverse_transform.
  • GroupedScaler — grouped/trended/windowed transforms; module functions grouped_transform, trended_transform, windowed_transform, lag_by_days, decomposed_transform, calendar_features.
  • DatasetBuilder — add_numeric(name, values) / add_categorical(name, values) / build() → schema summary.
  • IndexMapper — string ↔ code mapping: fit, transform, inverse_transform, get_index, get_name, get_all_names.

items.title: Missing-value semantics
items.text: None and NaN = missing (NaN normalized at ingestion). Missing in → missing out; imputation is opt-in; unseen categorical levels map to missing; degenerate scalings produce missing, not inf. Time-series transforms drop incomplete rows and warn with the count.

items.title: Generator
items.text:
generate(...) — the adjustable benchmark generator with known ground truth (group/hierarchy signal knobs). See docs/field-notes.md for the research context.

Next: Model for the tree itself, or Metrics for evaluation.

items.title: Class reference
items.text:
Full docstrings and every method: the full generated API.

DatasetBuilder(n_category=None, na_policy='allow', digits=None, add_intercept=False) — ingest any raw columns into the typed dataset. add_categorical(name, values), add_numeric(name, values), build() → {"columns", "dtypes", "na_counts", "n_rows", "n_cols"}.

Encoders — all: fit(values) → transform(values) (dict of columns), levels(); None = missing, unseen → missing. Constructors vary per encoder (see the table above); every arg is optional.

VariableScaler(normalize) / GroupedScaler — fit / transform / inverse_transform (invertible by construction).

IndexMapper — fit, transform, inverse_transform, get_index, get_name, get_all_names.

items.title: A real example (churn)
items.text:
from mltreelib import DatasetBuilder, OneHotEncoder, load_dataset

d = load_dataset("churn")            # the typed dataset dict
cols = d["columns"]
print(f"churn: {d['n_rows']} rows x {d['n_cols']} cols; "
      f"na_counts (state) = {d['na_counts']['state']}")

b = DatasetBuilder(n_category=5, na_policy="impute")
b.add_categorical("state", [str(v) for v in cols["state"]])
b.add_numeric("account_length", [float(v) for v in cols["account_length"]])
b.add_numeric("total_day_charge", [float(v) for v in cols["total_day_charge"]])
d2 = b.build()
print(f"build(): {d2['n_rows']} rows x {d2['n_cols']} cols; "
      f"dtypes={d2['dtypes']}; na_counts={d2['na_counts']}")

enc = OneHotEncoder()
enc.fit([str(v) for v in cols["state"]])
X = enc.transform([str(v) for v in cols["state"]])
print(f"OneHotEncoder on state: fit -> {len(enc.levels())} levels; "
      f"transform -> dict of {len(X)} columns x {len(next(iter(X.values())))} rows")

build(): 5000 rows x 3 cols; dtypes={'state': 'categorical',
  'account_length': 'numeric', 'total_day_charge': 'numeric'};
  na_counts={'state': 0, 'account_length': 0, 'total_day_charge': 0}
OneHotEncoder on state: fit -> 51 levels; transform -> dict of 51 columns
  x 5000 rows

load_dataset returns the built typed dataset (name, columns, dtypes, na_counts, n_rows, n_cols) — the same schema DatasetBuilder.build() produces, which is why the two interoperate.

items.title: API reference — Metrics
items.text:
Metrics — evaluation reports, curves, scorecards, stability and distances. Everything returns plain structures (numeric series + summary scalars); the library never plots — rendering lives in mltreelib.plots (matplotlib as an optional extra) and the Visualization example. Charts on these docs are click-to-zoom.

Unless noted, classification inputs take scores/probabilities with positive class y > 0.5; ties sweep together in stable order.

items.title: Reports
items.text:
• Metrics().regression(y_true, y_pred) → n, n_missing, mean_error, bias, mae, mad, mape, rmse, r2, max_error, explained_variance, plus a deciles table (decile, n, mean_error, mae, mape) — calibration by tentile, not just accuracy. Missing-aware.
  • Metrics().classification(y_true, y_pred) — integer class labels — n, n_missing, n_classes, accuracy, macro_precision/recall/f1, per_class, confusion matrix.
  • Metrics().regression_by_group(keys, y_true, y_pred) — regression report per group key.

items.title: Ranking & calibration curves
items.text: call returns roc_curve(y, scores) {"points": [[fpr, tpr], ...], "auc"} — trapezoid over the empirical curve pr_curve(y, scores) {"points": [[recall, precision], ...], "average_precision"} — step-wise AP (sklearn convention) gain_curve(y, scores) {"points": [[population_fraction, capture_rate], ...]} lift_curve(y, scores) {"points": [[population_fraction, lift], ...]} — lift = capture / fraction ks_statistic(y, scores) {"points": [[fpr, tpr, score], ...], "ks", "score_at_ks", "tpr_at_ks", "fpr_at_ks"} decile_table(y, scores, n_buckets=10) [{"decile", "n", "avg_score", "events", "event_rate", "cum_capture", "cum_event_rate", "lift"}] — decile 1 = top scores (kds/PerfScoreCard profile; response + cumulative response at decile granularity) calibration(y, scores, n_bins=10) {"bins": [{"left", "right", "mean_score", "observed", "n"}]} — equal-width over [0, 1], edge-clipped, empty bins omitted

items.title: Probability & margin scores
items.text:
• log_loss(y, probs) — mean log loss (probabilities clip to (1e-15, 1−1e-15)).
  • brier_score(y, probs) — mean squared probability error.
  • hinge_loss(y, decision) — mean hinge over signed margins (labels map to ±1).

items.title: Classification scorecard
items.text:
Metrics().classification_scores(y_true, y_pred) — single-label binary or multiclass, labels = sorted distinct union of truth and predictions:

n, n_classes, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, precision/recall/f1 × (macro|micro|weighted), mcc (Gorodkin multiclass Matthews), jaccard × (macro|micro|weighted), hamming_loss, zero_one_loss.

items.title: Multilabel scorecard
items.text:
Metrics().multilabel_scores(y_true, y_scores) — rows are instances, columns labels, entries > 0.5 positive; the raw entries double as ranking scores:

subset_accuracy, hamming_loss, precision/recall/f1 × (micro|macro|samples), label_ranking_ap, coverage_error. Rows with no true labels are skipped in the samples averages and ranking metrics.

items.title: Agreement
items.text: Metrics().weighted_kappa(y_true, y_pred, weights="quadratic"|"linear"|"none") — Cohen's kappa over the sorted distinct labels; 1 = perfect agreement (PerfScoreCard's weighted kappas).

items.title: Stability (scorecard monitoring)
items.text: Metrics().stability_index(reference, current, n_bins=10) → {"psi": float, "bins": [{"left", "right", "reference_share", "current_share", "contribution"}]} — the Population Stability Index (equal-width bins over the reference range, zero shares floored at 1e-6). CSI is the same call on a feature column instead of scores.

items.title: Model comparison
items.text: Metrics().double_lift(y_true, scores_a, scores_b, n_buckets=10) → [{"bucket", "n", "actual", "pred_a", "pred_b"}] — equal-count buckets by model A's ranking (CAS monograph double-lift chart; the additive vs ratio display is a plotting concern — plots.plot_double_lift(model_type=...)).

items.title: Distances
items.text: Metrics().pairwise_distances(a, b, metric="euclidean", p=2.0) → len(a) × len(b) matrix. Metrics: euclidean, manhattan, chebyshev, minkowski (power p), cosine, correlation, hamming, jaccard (binary presence). Zero-variance rows → correlation distance 1.0; zero vectors → cosine distance 1.0; both-empty → jaccard 0.0.

items.title: Plotting (mltreelib.plots)
items.text:
Optional layer, installed with pip install mltreelib[plotting] (matplotlib + pygraphviz + seaborn; each function takes ax=None, returns Axes): plot_roc, plot_pr, plot_cumulative_gain, plot_lift, plot_ks, plot_decile, plot_calibration, plot_response, plot_double_lift, plot_psi.

from mltreelib import Metrics, plots
r = Metrics().roc_curve(y_test, scores)
plots.plot_ks(y_test, scores)          # click the figure in these docs to zoom

Time-series metrics (MAPE/SMAPE variants, MASE, pinball for quantiles, Tweedie/Poisson deviance with the GLM leaves) are parked with their feature work.

Next: Data or Model.

items.title: The Metrics class
items.text:
Metrics() — no constructor args; every method is a complete report. Missing pairs are dropped and counted in n_missing. Full docstrings: the full generated API.

family methods reports classification(y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None), classification_scores(y_true, scores), regression(y_true, y_pred), classification_by_group(keys, ...), regression_by_group(keys, y_true, y_pred) curves roc_curve, pr_curve, gain_curve, lift_curve, decile_table, calibration probability & margin log_loss, brier_score, hinge_loss scorecards ks_statistic, weighted_kappa(y_true, y_pred, rev, power) multilabel multilabel_scores(y_true, y_pred) distances pairwise_distances(a, b, metric, p=2) stability stability_index(reference, current, n_bins=10) model comparison double_lift(y_true, a, b, model_type)

items.title: A real example (churn)
items.text:
from mltreelib import Metrics, load_dataset

cols = load_dataset("churn")["columns"]
y = [1 if str(v) == "Yes" else 0 for v in cols["CustomerChurned"]]
print(f"churn: 5000 rows; event rate {sum(y)/len(y):.3f} ({sum(y)} churned)")
scores = [float(v) for v in cols["total_day_charge"]]   # a (silly) risk score
med = sorted(scores)[len(scores) // 2]
pred = [1 if s >= med else 0 for s in scores]

rep = Metrics().classification(y, pred,
                               probabilities=[min(1.0, s / 80.0) for s in scores])
print(f"classification: accuracy={rep['accuracy']:.3f} "
      f"macro_f1={rep['macro_f1']:.3f} auc={rep['auc']:.3f} "
      f"logloss={rep['logloss']:.3f} brier={rep['brier']:.3f}")
mins = [float(v) for v in cols["total_day_minutes"]]
fit = [s / 0.17 for s in scores]                        # charge = 0.17 * minutes
rr = Metrics().regression(mins, fit)
print(f"regression: n={rr['n']} rmse={rr['rmse']:.2f} mae={rr['mae']:.2f} "
      f"r2={rr['r2']:.3f} mape={rr['mape']:.2f}")
gr = Metrics().regression_by_group([str(v) for v in cols["state"]], mins, fit)
print(f"regression_by_group: {len(gr)} groups (keyed by group)")

churn: 5000 rows; event rate 0.141 (707 churned)
classification: accuracy=0.531 macro_f1=0.462 auc=0.640 logloss=0.545 brier=0.176
regression: n=5000 rmse=0.02 mae=0.01 r2=1.000 mape=0.01
regression_by_group: 51 groups (keyed by group)

The classification report carries accuracy, macro_precision/recall/f1, per_class, confusion and (with probabilities) auc, logloss, brier. The regression report carries n, n_missing, mean_error, bias, mae, mad, mape, rmse, r2, max_error, explained_variance and the deciles error profile; the grouped version returns one such report per group (dict keyed by group). Full output shapes on real data: the Metrics & plots showcase.

items.title: API reference — Model
items.text: ModelTree — the tree: greedy splits by fitted-leaf SSE reduction, linear or mean leaves, NA-aware (learned split directions + NA-indicator leaf terms). Rust core is the source of truth; this page mirrors it.

items.title: Constructor
items.text:
ModelTree(
    max_depth=4, min_rows=10, min_gain=1e-9,
    leaf_cols="all",        # "all" | "path" — columns available to leaf models
    leaf="linear",          # "linear"|"mean"|"median"|"quantile"|"huber"
    tau=0.5,                # the quantile for leaf="quantile"
    l2=0.1, l1=0.0,         # ridge on leaf coefficients (l1 off by default)
    monotone=[],            # per column: 0 | +1 | -1
    interaction_groups=[],  # [[col, ...], ...] — paths may not mix groups
    min_relevance=None,     # relevance threshold for column screening
    gain="sse",             # regression: "sse"|"friedman_mse"|"absolute_error"|"huber"|"poisson"|"sdr";
                            # class: "entropy"|"gini"|"gain_ratio"|"twoing"; or callable
    split_precision=0.001, # numeric candidate grid (thousandths); None = exact unique scan
    cat_order="frequency_desc",  # "frequency_desc" | "target_mean" | [level codes]
    cat_search="cumulative",     # "cumulative" | "single_vs_rest" | "both"
    leaf_digest=True,       # keep each leaf's t-digest (quantile() needs it)
    verbose=0,              # 0 silent | 1 per depth | 2 per node (training_log)
    alpha=0.0,              # min child weight share (grf's alpha); 0 = off
    imbalance_penalty=0.0,  # subtract penalty*(1/n_l + 1/n_r) from the gain
    col_sample=None,        # per-node random column fraction (forest spirit)
    seed=42,                # column-subset seed (deterministic)
    prune="none",           # "none" | "bic" | "mdl" — bottom-up cost pruning
)

The gain family is sample-weight aware end to end: weighted class masses for entropy/gini/gain_ratio/twoing, weighted moments for sdr/SSE, and a custom gain_fn(left, right) receives lazy (y, w) pair slices of the two sides (higher = better). gain_ratio is C4.5 (information gain ÷ split information), sdr is the model-tree standard-deviation reduction, twoing is Breiman's balanced-contrast rule.

Defaults are the arena bake-off winner (see Benchmarks) — linear leaves at shallow depth with a small ridge (l2) penalty. l1 (lasso/elastic) is available but off by default: coordinate descent is slow inside the split scan and the accuracy gain over ridge is marginal. Turning regularization fully off (l1=l2=0) on raw scales is a known blowup mode — keep the ridge unless you standardize your inputs.

items.title: Split search — per dtype, no encoding
items.text:
Categorical columns are levels as-is (dtypes declares them; a distinct value is a level), NAs route as-is. Nothing is ever encoded on the growth path — the encoders in Data are pipeline tools for feeding sklearn and friends, never invoked by the tree. Binary level partitions (cat_search) are built along cat_order; multiway partitions are reserved for a later build. gain picks the split-quality function: the built-ins scan on summary stats, a custom gain_fn(left_y, right_y) -> float receives lazy y-slices per candidate (higher = better; sees y values only). Float columns scan candidates on the split_precision grid (thresholds are grid values; prediction rounds to the same grid), None restores the exact scan.

m = ModelTree(max_depth=1, min_rows=5, gain="entropy", cat_search="cumulative")
m.fit(x, y, dtypes=["categorical"])
m.predict([[0.0], [1.0], [2.0]])

categorical fit: pred(0,1,2) = [0.0, 5.0, 5.0]     # {0} | {1,2} partition
grid threshold: 1.3 (on the grid: True)

items.title: Quantiles and the training log
items.text:
leaf_digest=True keeps a t-digest in every leaf (weighted targets) — quantile(x, tau) then answers any τ after the fit (median now, p90 later, no refit). leaf_digest=False drops the digests (leaner; quantile returns NaN). training_log() returns the scan log when verbose > 0: scan config, per-depth/per-node candidate counts, timings.

mq = ModelTree(max_depth=1, min_rows=5)          # leaf_digest=True default
mq.fit(xg, yg)
mq.quantile([[1.25]], 0.5), mq.quantile([[2.25]], 0.9)

quantile 0.5: 0.0 | p90: 1.0
training_log: 3 lines; first: depth 0: nodes=1 rows=60 candidates=3 scan_ms=0

items.title: Fitting & predicting
items.text: method returns notes fit(x, y, w=None, dtypes=None) self rows of float/None (None = missing); w = row weights (0 = row ignored); dtypes = per column "numeric"/"categorical" (levels as-is); rows with None target drop predict(x) list[float] missing cells route by the learned NA direction; never panics on short rows quantile(x, tau) list[float] conditional τ-quantile per row from the leaf t-digests

items.title: Reading the model
items.text: method returns notes __repr__() str rpart-style text (print(model)); refuses to print an unfitted tree to_dot() str Graphviz DOT — render with pygraphviz/graphviz (layout is graphviz's job) splits() list[dict] {col, threshold, missing_left, gain} per split (col is the column name) leaves() list[dict] one flat dict per leaf: cols, coef, na_coef, intercept, n, mean, std, min, max, quantiles split_paths() list[list[str]] split column names per root→leaf path (constraint verification) n_leaves() int terminal node count profile() list[dict] per-depth fit diagnostics: depth, nodes, rows, cols, candidates, group_ns, scan_ns, leaf_ns

items.title: Explaining predictions
items.text:
method returns notes break_down(row) dict DALEX-style decomposition of one prediction: {"baseline", "steps": [[column, contribution], ...], "residual", "prediction"} feature_importance() list[(name, share)] each column's share of total split gain (rpart's variable importance); sorted descending, shares sum to 1

Break-down contract: baseline is the training mean; each split on the row's route contributes (child node mean − parent node mean) to its column in decision-path order; residual is the within-leaf model adjustment (0 for mean leaves). They telescope exactly:

baseline + sum(contributions) + residual == prediction

Routing in break_down is identical to predict (inclusive threshold comparison; missing cells follow the split's learned missing direction), so the explanation always matches the prediction.

items.title: Constraints
items.text:
• monotone[j] = +1 → predictions never decrease in column j (-1: never increase). Enforced at split choice and in leaf coefficients (linear leaves carry effects in their coefficients; split checks alone don't fire when there are no splits).
  • interaction_groups → every root-to-leaf path splits only columns of one group (LightGBM-style interaction constraints).

Both are validated against reference implementations in examples/constraints_check.py (R gbm's var.monotone, LightGBM's interaction_constraints).

items.title: Inspection via text output
items.text:
print(model) reproduces rpart's print byte-for-byte: binary-heap node numbering, 2·depth indent, x< t / x>=t labels, format(signif(x,7)) columns, * terminal markers. Node ids in to_dot() match the text print.

items.title: API reference — Evaluation reports
items.text: What Metrics returns, field by field — the contract every learner is scored under. Reports are plain dicts; missing pairs are dropped from the math and counted in n_missing, never hidden.

items.title: Metrics().regression(y_true, y_pred) → dict
items.text: field meaning n, n_missing observed pairs; dropped missing pairs mean_error mean(actual − fitted) — signed bias mean_pred / mean_true (1.0 = unbiased) mae, mad mean / median absolute deviation mape absolute % error, non-zero targets only rmse, r2, max_error the usual explained_variance 1 − Var(error)/Var(y) deciles per-target-decile error profile — the DAR "bathtub" view

items.title: Metrics().classification(y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None) → dict
items.text: field meaning n, n_missing, n_classes observed pairs; classes seen accuracy overall accuracy macro_precision/recall/f1 unweighted mean over classes per_class precision/recall/f1/support per class confusion counts matrix auc, logloss, brier only with probabilities (P(class 1))

items.title: Grouped reports
items.text:
classification_by_group(keys, ...) / regression_by_group(keys, y_true, y_pred) return one report per group, as a dict keyed by the group label — the format ModelTree's group API consumes.

Real values for every field on real data: the Metrics & plots showcase and the Metrics page example.

items.title: API reference — Data
items.text: Typed ingest, the synthetic generator, dataset helpers and column screening. Guide with real examples: Data.

items.title: generate
items.text:
pythongenerate((n_rows=10000, n_numeric=5, cardinalities=None, hierarchy_levels=3, branching=None, group_effect_strength=0.5, hierarchy_effect_strength=0.3, interaction_strength=0.2, noise=0.1, task='regression', n_classes=2, tail_behavior='gaussian', missingness=0.0, seed=42)) Generate an adjustable benchmark dataset with known ground truth.

The knobs control how much signal lives in numeric effects, categorical levels, hierarchical groups and their interaction — so learners can be scored on structure recovery, not just accuracy. Deterministic for a given seed.

Args: n_rows: number of rows to generate. n_numeric: numeric feature columns; the first two carry linear signal. cardinalities: level count per categorical column (each >= 2). hierarchy_levels: depth of the categorical hierarchy (0 = none). branching: child count per hierarchy level (last value repeats). group_effect_strength: scale of categorical level effects. hierarchy_effect_strength: scale of hierarchy node effects. interaction_strength: scale of the numeric x categorical interaction. noise: scale of the residual noise. task: "regression" or "classification". n_classes: class count for classification (equal-frequency cuts). tail_behavior: "gaussian", "heavy" (Student-t residuals) or "bathtub" (noise grows with the signal — the DAR motivation). missingness: fraction of feature cells set to missing, in [0, 1). seed: RNG seed.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values, None = missing), target, labels (classification only) and truth — the true effects plus truth["variance"], the realized variance share of each component.

Raises: ValueError: invalid parameter combination.

items.title: load_dataset
items.text:
pythonload_dataset((name: 'str') -> 'dict') Load one dataset as name/columns/dtypes/n_rows/n_cols.

columns maps column name to a list with None for missing values; dtypes is "numeric" or "categorical" (strings/dictionaries).

items.title: list_datasets
items.text: pythonlist_datasets(() -> 'list[str]') Names of the available benchmark datasets (parquet stems).

items.title: summarize
items.text:
pythonsummarize((values)) Summary of observed values, with missing counts shown by default.

NAs and NaNs are excluded from the statistics but always reported in n_missing — nothing is silently hidden.

Args: values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: dict with count (observed), n_missing, sum, mean, std, min, q1, median, q3, max (NaN for the statistics of an all-missing input).

items.title: winnow
items.text:
pythonwinnow((x, y, w=None, min_relevance=0.05)) Winnowing: screen columns by univariate relevance against the target and keep the relevant ones (the cheap pre-split screening LightGBM's docs call feature pre-filtering / winnowing).

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing. y: targets (rows with None targets or zero weight are dropped). w: optional row weights. min_relevance: keep columns with relevance >= this (default 0.05).

Returns: {"kept": [column indices], "relevance": [score per column]}.

items.title: DatasetBuilder
items.text:
pythonclass DatasetBuilder((n_category=None, na_policy='allow', digits=None, add_intercept=False)) Ingest any data into the typed dataset.

Owns the ingestion semantics: n_category category inference, explicit NA policy, digit rounding and an optional intercept column. Missing is None or NaN — both are counted in na_counts, and filling is opt-in only.

Args (constructor): n_category: integral numeric columns with at most this many distinct levels become categorical; values < 1 mean a fraction of rows (None = no inference). na_policy: "allow" (keep missing), "drop" (drop rows containing any missing) or "impute" (numeric mean, categorical mode). digits: round floats to this many decimal places (None = no rounding). add_intercept: append a constant 1.0 column named intercept.

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_categorical
items.text:
pythonadd_categorical((self, /, name, values)) Add a categorical column from strings; the vocabulary is first-seen order. None = missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one level per row (None = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.add_numeric
items.text:
pythonadd_numeric((self, /, name, values)) Add a numeric column. NaN is treated as missing.

Args: name: column name. values: one value per row (None/NaN = missing).

items.title: DatasetBuilder.build
items.text:
pythonbuild((self, /)) Build the typed dataset with the configured policies applied.

Returns: dict with columns (name -> values), dtypes ("numeric" or "categorical"), na_counts (missing per column), n_rows, n_cols.

Raises: ValueError: inconsistent column lengths, duplicate names, invalid policy usage (e.g. "drop" removing every row).

items.title: API reference — Encoders & scalers
items.text: Pipeline tools for feeding downstream algorithms (sklearn and friends) — never invoked by the tree. Guide: Data.

items.title: IndexMapper
items.text: pythonclass IndexMapper(()) Categorical string <-> stable code mapping (sklearn-style fit/transform).

items.title: IndexMapper.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, name, values)) Learn the vocabulary of name (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets it.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_all_names
items.text:
pythonget_all_names((self, /, name)) All fitted levels in code order.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_index
items.text:
pythonget_index((self, /, name, value)) Code for one level (None when the level is unseen).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted.

items.title: IndexMapper.get_name
items.text:
pythonget_name((self, /, name, index)) Level for one code.

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.inverse_transform
items.text:
pythoninverse_transform((self, /, name, codes)) Map codes back to their string levels.

Args: name: fitted column name. codes: codes per row (None = missing).

Returns: string levels (None where the code is missing).

Raises: ValueError: column not fitted or code out of range.

items.title: IndexMapper.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, name, values)) Codes for values; unseen levels map to None (missing).

items.title: VariableScaler
items.text:
pythonclass VariableScaler(()) Per-column distributional scaling — each variable transformed independently (legacy VariableTransformation semantics).

Same strategy names as GroupedScaler, applied per column, with exact inverse_transform. None/NaN are missing and pass through as missing; degenerate scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: VariableScaler.fit
items.text:
pythonfit((self, /, columns, strategy)) Fit all columns at once under the given strategy.

Args: columns: {name: values} for every column to scale (None/NaN = missing; counted in each column's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see GroupedScaler).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy.

items.title: VariableScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
pythoninverse_transform((self, /, name, values)) Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: VariableScaler.transform
items.text:
pythontransform((self, /, name, values)) Scale one fitted column's values.

Args: name: fitted column name. values: numeric values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: scaled values; None for missing inputs and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or unknown column.

items.title: GroupedScaler
items.text:
pythonclass GroupedScaler(()) Fit/transform group distributional scaling with exact inverse (sklearn-shaped: fit once, then transform / inverse_transform).

Strategies: centered family — "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr"; ratio family — "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range". Missing in -> missing out; degenerate (zero) scales give missing, never inf.

items.title: GroupedScaler.fit
items.text:
pythonfit((self, /, keys, values, strategy)) Fit group statistics of values under the given strategy.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; counted in each group's n_missing). strategy: strategy name (see the class docstring).

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.inverse_transform
items.text:
pythoninverse_transform((self, /, keys, values)) Exact inverse of transform under the fitted statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: previously transformed values.

Returns: original-scale values (up to floating-point error).

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: GroupedScaler.transform
items.text:
pythontransform((self, /, keys, values)) Scale values against the fitted group statistics.

Args: keys: group label per row. values: numeric value per row.

Returns: scaled values; None for missing key/value, unseen groups and degenerate scales.

Raises: ValueError: not fitted or mismatched lengths.

items.title: BaseNEncoder
items.text: pythonclass BaseNEncoder((base)) Base-N / binary encoding: each level becomes its base-base digits as indicator columns (base = 2 is the classic Binary encoder). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen and missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values)) Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: BaseNEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Returns {digit name: indicator list}.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder
items.text:
pythonclass CatBoostEncoder((prior, permutations, seed)) CatBoost-style ordered target statistics — the leakage-safe flavour.

fit_transform gives each row the running statistic of its level using only rows earlier in a shuffled order: (sum_y_prefix + prior * global) / (n_prefix + 1), averaged over permutations seeded passes. The same level gets different values in different rows — that row-dependence is the anti-leakage mechanism. transform (new data) uses prior-smoothed fitted level means.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit prior-smoothed level means (used by transform on new data).

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform
items.text: pythonfit_transform((self, /, values, y)) Leakage-safe ordered encodings of the training rows themselves.

items.title: CatBoostEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Encode new rows from the fitted level means; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: CountEncoder
items.text: pythonclass CountEncoder((normalize)) Count / frequency encoding: occurrence count per category (normalize gives the share of rows). Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen levels give 0.0; missing stays missing.

items.title: CountEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values)) Fit counts on values.

items.title: CountEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Count (or share) per row; unseen -> 0.0, missing -> None.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder
items.text: pythonclass EmbeddingEncoder((dim, lr, epochs, seed, task)) NN-style learned embeddings per category: a small embedding table and a linear head trained by SGD, one table per categorical feature. Task: both — softmax head for classification; for regression a ReLU output when all fitted targets are non-negative, linear otherwise. transform returns the embeddings, predict the trained head. Unseen levels give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y, n_classes=None)) Train on (values, y); n_classes is inferred for classification when omitted, ignored for regression.

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.predict
items.text: pythonpredict((self, /, values)) Predictions of the trained head (class label or activated value).

items.title: EmbeddingEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Learned embedding per row (None = missing, zeros = unseen).

items.title: HashingEncoder
items.text: pythonclass HashingEncoder((n_buckets)) Hashed one-hot: levels are hashed into n_buckets indicator columns, so unseen levels still land somewhere. Deterministic.

items.title: HashingEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Returns {bucket name: indicator list}.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder
items.text: pythonclass JamesSteinEncoder(()) James-Stein encoding: level means shrunk toward the grand mean with B = max(0, 1 - ((L - 3) * sigma2) / sum((mean_i - global)^2)); fewer than three levels collapse to the grand mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit shrunk means on (values, y).

items.title: JamesSteinEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Shrunk mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder
items.text: pythonclass LeaveOneOutEncoder(()) Leave-one-out encoding: fit_transform gives each row its level's mean target without that row (leakage-aware); transform on new data uses the full fitted level mean. Task: both. Unseen -> global mean; missing -> None.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.fit_transform
items.text: pythonfit_transform((self, /, values, y)) Row-level means excluding each row's own target.

items.title: LeaveOneOutEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Full fitted level means for new rows.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder
items.text: pythonclass MEstimatorEncoder((m)) M-estimate encoding: (sum_y + m * global) / (n_level + m) — target smoothing with fixed strength m. Task: both (leaky on training data; prefer CatBoostEncoder or LeaveOneOutEncoder there). Unseen -> global; missing -> None.

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit smoothed level means on (values, y).

items.title: MEstimatorEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Smoothed mean per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: OneHotEncoder
items.text: pythonclass OneHotEncoder(()) One-hot expansion: one indicator column per fitted level (first-seen order). Missing values and levels unseen at fit produce an all-zero row.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values)) Learn the levels (first-seen order). Re-fitting resets them.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.levels
items.text: pythonlevels((self, /)) Fitted levels, in column order.

items.title: OneHotEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Returns {level: indicator list}; unseen/missing rows are all-zero.

items.title: QuantileEncoder
items.text: pythonclass QuantileEncoder((q, smoothing)) Quantile encoding: each level becomes its smoothed target quantile (default median), w * level_quantile + (1 - w) * global_quantile with w = n / (n + smoothing). Task: regression. Unseen -> global quantile; missing -> None.

items.title: QuantileEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit quantiles on (values, y).

items.title: QuantileEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Smoothed quantile per row; unseen -> global, missing -> None.

items.title: SumEncoder
items.text: pythonclass SumEncoder(()) Sum contrast coding: k-1 columns; level i < k-1 gets +1 in column i, the last level gets -1 across all columns. Task: both (unsupervised). Unseen rows give zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: SumEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values)) Fit the level vocabulary on values.

items.title: SumEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Contrast row per row (None = missing).

items.title: TargetEncoder
items.text:
pythonclass TargetEncoder((smoothing)) Smoothed target encoding (fitted-mean flavour).

w * level_mean + (1 - w) * global_mean with w = n / (n + smoothing). Leaky on training data (the row's own target is in its level mean) — prefer CatBoostEncoder.fit_transform for training features. Unseen levels fall back to the global mean; missing stays missing.

items.title: TargetEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y)) Fit level means on (values, y).

items.title: TargetEncoder.prior
items.text: pythonprior((self, /)) The global mean used as the unseen-level fallback.

items.title: TargetEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) Encode values; unseen -> global mean, missing -> None.

items.title: TfidfEncoder
items.text: pythonclass TfidfEncoder((normalize)) Class-level TF-IDF: each category becomes a vector over the target classes — tf(v,j) = count(v,j)/count(v) times idf(j) = ln(1 + n/(1 + count(j))) + 1; normalize scales each level vector to unit L2 norm. Task: classification. Unseen levels fall back to the global class shares; missing stays missing.

items.title: TfidfEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y, n_classes)) Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: TfidfEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) One class-space vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: WoEEncoder
items.text: pythonclass WoEEncoder((prior)) Weight of Evidence (credit-risk classic): one-vs-rest ln(distr_j(v) / distr_not_j(v)) per category, smoothed with additive prior. Task: classification. Positive = over-representation of the class in that level. Unseen levels give neutral zeros; missing stays missing.

items.title: WoEEncoder.fit
items.text: pythonfit((self, /, values, y, n_classes)) Fit class counts on (values, y, n_classes).

items.title: WoEEncoder.transform
items.text: pythontransform((self, /, values)) One WoE vector per row (None = missing).

items.title: API reference — Feature functions
items.text: Grouped/trended/windowed transforms, lags and calendar parts. Guide: Data processing.

items.title: grouped_scale
items.text:
pythongrouped_scale((keys, values, strategy='zscore')) One-shot group scaling: fit on (keys, values) and transform the same rows.

Each row's value is scaled by its group's summary under strategy (centered family like "zscore" or ratio family like "mean"; see GroupedScaler for the full list and the exact inverse).

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing). strategy: one of "zscore", "min-max", "median-iqr", "mean-iqr", "median-qd", "median-std", "median-range", "mean-range", "min-qd", "min-iqr", "min", "max", "mean", "median", "iqr", "qd", "std", "range".

Returns: scaled values; rows with a missing key/value, an unseen group or a degenerate (zero) scale give None — missing in, missing out.

Raises: ValueError: unknown strategy or mismatched lengths.

items.title: grouped_transform
items.text:
pythongrouped_transform((keys, values, kind='mean')) Per-row group summary of values within groups defined by keys.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = missing). values: numeric value per row (None/NaN = missing; excluded from the group statistics but counted in each group's n_missing). kind: "mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1" or "q3".

Returns: the summary of each row's group; rows with a missing key/value or an unseen group give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown kind or mismatched lengths.

items.title: trended_transform
items.text:
pythontrended_transform((keys, dates, values, granularity='year_month', kind='mean', hemisphere='north')) Grouped summary trended at a time granularity.

Each row gets the summary of its (key x time-bucket) cell — e.g. with granularity "year_month" and kind "mean", the row's key-and-month mean. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). granularity: bucket spec joined by "_" from {year, halfyear, season, quarter, month, week, weekday, day} — e.g. "year_month", "year_week", "month_weekday". kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: per-row cell summaries; incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: unknown granularity/kind/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: windowed_transform
items.text:
pythonwindowed_transform((keys, dates, values, window_days=7, kind='mean', include_current=True)) Trailing-window aggregation per key over day windows.

Each row summarizes the observed values of its key in a window of window_days days; incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). window_days: window length in days (>= 1); covering the window_days days ending at the row's date, or strictly earlier days when include_current is false. kind: summary kind ("mean", "sum", "std", "count", "min", "max", "median", "q1", "q3"). include_current: include the row's own date in the window.

Returns: per-row window summaries; None for incomplete rows and for empty/all-missing windows.

Raises: ValueError: window_days == 0, unknown kind, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: lag_by_days
items.text:
pythonlag_by_days((keys, dates, values, lag_days)) Lag values by whole days within each key (day granularity).

Each row receives the value of its key at date - lag_days; duplicate (key, date) rows keep the last occurrence. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). lag_days: lag in whole days (0 returns the row's own value).

Returns: lagged values; None where no source row exists.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: decomposed_transform
items.text:
pythondecomposed_transform((keys, dates, values, season_granularity='month', trend_window=3, hemisphere='north')) Additive decomposition, following the statsmodels seasonal_decompose (additive) convention.

The trend is a centered moving average over each key's rows ordered by date; the seasonal component is the mean of (series - trend) per (key, season bucket), estimated from rows with a complete trend window. Incomplete rows (missing key/date/value) are dropped from estimation and reported via a warning.

Args: keys: series label per row (None = missing). dates: ISO date strings per row (None = missing). values: numeric values per row (None/NaN = missing). season_granularity: bucket spec for the seasonal component (e.g. "month", "weekday" — same vocabulary as trended_transform). trend_window: centered moving-average window in rows (>= 1). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (affects the season component).

Returns: dict with detrended (series - trend), deseasonalized (series - seasonal) and residual (series - trend - seasonal); incomplete rows give None.

Raises: ValueError: trend_window == 0, unknown granularity/hemisphere, unparseable date or mismatched lengths.

items.title: calendar_features
items.text:
pythoncalendar_features((dates, hemisphere='north')) Calendar features for ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD or timestamp prefix).

Produces year, halfyear, quarter, month, week (ISO), iso_year, weekday (0 = Monday), day, day_of_year, season and weekend as numeric parts, ready for tree learners.

Args: dates: ISO date strings or timestamps (None = missing). hemisphere: "north" or "south" (southern shifts the season by six months).

Returns: dict of 11 feature lists aligned with dates; rows with a missing date give None features.

Raises: ValueError: unparseable date or unknown hemisphere.

items.title: API reference — Metrics
items.text: Complete evaluation reports at once. Guides: Metrics, Evaluation reports.

items.title: Metrics
items.text: pythonclass Metrics(()) One metrics class computing complete reports at once — the yardstick every learner is measured with. Task: both. Pairs with a missing/NaN side are dropped from the math and reported in n_missing, never hidden.

items.title: Metrics.brier_score
items.text:
pythonbrier_score((self, /, y_true, probs)) Brier score of probability predictions. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). probs: predicted probabilities.

Returns: mean squared probability error.

items.title: Metrics.calibration
items.text:
pythoncalibration((self, /, y_true, scores, n_bins=10)) Calibration (reliability) bins: mean predicted score vs observed frequency per bin. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities. n_bins: equal-width bins over [0, 1] (default 10).

Returns: {"bins": [{"left", "right", "mean_score", "observed", "n"}]} (empty bins omitted; scores clip into edge bins).

items.title: Metrics.classification
items.text:
pythonclassification((self, /, y_true, y_pred, probabilities=None)) Complete classification report: accuracy, macro averages, per-class precision/recall/f1/support, confusion matrix — and with probabilities (P(class 1)) also logloss, brier and ROC-AUC.

Args: y_true: integer class labels (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: predicted labels (None/NaN = missing). probabilities: P(class 1) per row; enables the probabilistic metrics.

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths, non-integer labels or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.classification_by_group
items.text:
pythonclassification_by_group((self, /, keys, y_true, y_pred)) Classification report per group key (sorted by key). Task: classification.

Args: keys: group label per row (rows with missing key/labels skip). y_true: integer class labels. y_pred: integer class labels.

Returns: {group: classification_report}.

items.title: Metrics.classification_scores
items.text:
pythonclassification_scores((self, /, y_true, y_pred)) Single-label classification scorecard (binary or multiclass). Task: classification.

Args: y_true: integer-like labels. y_pred: integer-like labels.

Returns: {"n", "n_classes", "accuracy", "balanced_accuracy", "precision_macro/micro/weighted", "recall_*", "f1_*", "mcc", "jaccard_macro/micro/weighted", "hamming_loss", "zero_one_loss"}.

items.title: Metrics.decile_table
items.text:
pythondecile_table((self, /, y_true, scores, n_buckets=10)) Decile profile (kds/PerfScoreCard decile table; modelplotpy response at decile granularity). Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities. n_buckets: equal-count buckets by score descending (default 10).

Returns: [{"decile", "n", "avg_score", "events", "event_rate", "cum_capture", "cum_event_rate", "lift"}, ...] (decile 1 = top).

items.title: Metrics.double_lift
items.text:
pythondouble_lift((self, /, y_true, scores_a, scores_b, n_buckets=10)) Double-lift table: actual vs model A vs model B along A's ranking (CAS monograph chart; additive vs ratio display is a plotting concern). Task: regression or classification.

Args: y_true: targets. scores_a: model A predictions (defines the ranking). scores_b: model B predictions. n_buckets: equal-count buckets (default 10).

Returns: [{"bucket", "n", "actual", "pred_a", "pred_b"}, ...].

items.title: Metrics.gain_curve
items.text:
pythongain_curve((self, /, y_true, scores)) Cumulative gains curve. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[population_fraction, capture_rate], ...]} (lift at a point = capture / fraction).

items.title: Metrics.hinge_loss
items.text:
pythonhinge_loss((self, /, y_true, decision)) Hinge loss over signed decision margins. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). decision: decision-function margins (signed).

Returns: mean hinge loss.

items.title: Metrics.ks_statistic
items.text:
pythonks_statistic((self, /, y_true, scores)) KS sweep + statistic + Score@KS. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[fpr, tpr, score], ...], "ks", "score_at_ks", "tpr_at_ks", "fpr_at_ks"}.

items.title: Metrics.lift_curve
items.text:
pythonlift_curve((self, /, y_true, scores)) Cumulative lift curve. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[population_fraction, lift], ...]} (lift = capture / population fraction).

items.title: Metrics.log_loss
items.text:
pythonlog_loss((self, /, y_true, probs)) Log loss of probability predictions. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). probs: predicted probabilities.

Returns: mean log loss.

items.title: Metrics.multilabel_scores
items.text:
pythonmultilabel_scores((self, /, y_true, y_scores)) Multilabel scorecard: rows are instances, columns are labels, entries

0.5 are positive (raw entries double as ranking scores). Task: multilabel classification.

Args: y_true: label matrix (rows x labels, 0/1). y_scores: prediction/score matrix (same shape).

Returns: {"n", "n_labels", "subset_accuracy", "hamming_loss", "precision_micro/macro/samples", "recall_*", "f1_*", "label_ranking_ap", "coverage_error"}.

items.title: Metrics.pairwise_distances
items.text:
pythonpairwise_distances((self, /, a, b, metric='euclidean', p=2.0)) Pairwise distances between two row sets. Task: any.

Args: a: first rows (rows x features). b: second rows (same width). metric: "euclidean" | "manhattan" | "chebyshev" | "minkowski" | "cosine" | "correlation" | "hamming" | "jaccard". p: Minkowski power (default 2.0).

Returns: len(a) x len(b) distance matrix.

items.title: Metrics.pr_curve
items.text:
pythonpr_curve((self, /, y_true, scores)) Precision-recall curve + average precision. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[recall, precision], ...], "average_precision": float}.

items.title: Metrics.regression
items.text:
pythonregression((self, /, y_true, y_pred)) Complete regression report: n, n_missing, mean_error (actual - fitted), bias (mean_pred / mean_true), mae, mad, mape (non-zero targets), rmse, r2, max_error, explained_variance and deciles — the DAR per-target-decile error profile (the bathtub view).

Args: y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: the full report as a dict.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.regression_by_group
items.text:
pythonregression_by_group((self, /, keys, y_true, y_pred)) Regression report per group (keys: dates, categories, ...) — the legacy per-key summary lineage. Rows with a missing key are ignored.

Args: keys: group label per row (None = ignored). y_true: actual values (None/NaN = missing). y_pred: fitted values (None/NaN = missing).

Returns: {group: regression report}, sorted by group.

Raises: ValueError: mismatched lengths or a group with no observed pairs.

items.title: Metrics.roc_curve
items.text:
pythonroc_curve((self, /, y_true, scores)) ROC curve + AUC. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: targets (positive = > 0.5). scores: predicted scores/probabilities.

Returns: {"points": [[fpr, tpr], ...], "auc": float}.

items.title: Metrics.stability_index
items.text:
pythonstability_index((self, /, reference, current, n_bins=10)) Stability index (PSI on scores, CSI on a feature column). Task: classification or regression monitoring.

Args: reference: reference-period values (bins derive from their range). current: current-period values. n_bins: equal-width bins (default 10).

Returns: {"psi": float, "bins": [{"left", "right", "reference_share", "current_share", "contribution"}, ...]}.

items.title: Metrics.weighted_kappa
items.text:
pythonweighted_kappa((self, /, y_true, y_pred, weights='quadratic')) Cohen's kappa with optional weights over the label scale. Task: classification.

Args: y_true: integer-like labels. y_pred: integer-like labels. weights: "none" | "linear" | "quadratic" (default "quadratic").

Returns: kappa (1 = perfect agreement).

items.title: API reference — ModelTree
items.text: The model tree: typed fit, split-search knobs, quantiles, training log. Guide: Model.

items.title: ModelTree
items.text: pythonclass ModelTree((max_depth=4, min_rows=10, min_gain=1e-09, leaf_cols='all', leaf='linear', tau=0.5, l2=0.1, l1=0.0, monotone=Ellipsis, interaction_groups=Ellipsis, min_relevance=None, gain=None, split_precision=Ellipsis, cat_order=None, cat_search='cumulative', leaf_digest=True, verbose=0, alpha=0.0, imbalance_penalty=0.0, col_sample=None, seed=42, prune='none', split_test='none', split_alpha=0.05, bonferroni=False)) Model tree: greedy splits by fitted-leaf SSE reduction, OLS or mean leaves, NA-aware (learned split directions + NA-indicator leaf terms). Task: regression.

items.title: ModelTree.break_down
items.text:
pythonbreak_down((self, /, row)) DALEX-style break-down of one prediction. Task: regression.

Args: row: one row of predictors (None = missing).

Returns: {"baseline", "steps": [[column_name, contribution], ...], "residual", "prediction"}; baseline + steps + residual == prediction.

items.title: ModelTree.feature_importance
items.text:
pythonfeature_importance((self, /)) Feature importance - each column's share of the total split gain (rpart's variable importance). Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: list of (column_name, share) sorted descending; shares sum to 1.

items.title: ModelTree.fit
items.text:
pythonfit((self, /, x, y, w=None, dtypes=None)) Fit the tree on row-major data. Task: regression.

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing (NA rows train). y: targets; None drops that row. w: optional per-row sample weights (row weightage); zero-weight rows are ignored. dtypes: optional per-column types — "numeric" (default) or "categorical" (values are level codes; the split search partitions levels, no encoding).

Returns: nothing; the fitted tree replaces the inner model.

items.title: ModelTree.leaves
items.text:
pythonleaves((self, /)) Fitted leaf models with their distribution stats. Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: one dict per leaf with cols, coef, na_coef, intercept, n, mean, std, min, max, quantiles.

items.title: ModelTree.n_leaves
items.text:
pythonn_leaves((self, /)) Number of leaves. Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: leaf count.

items.title: ModelTree.predict
items.text:
pythonpredict((self, /, x)) Predict for row-major data; NAs never block a prediction. Task: regression.

Args: x: rows of predictors; None entries are missing.

Returns: one predicted value per row.

items.title: ModelTree.profile
items.text:
pythonprofile((self, /)) Per-level timing profile (group/sort, scan, leaf fit). Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: one dict per depth level with depth, nodes, rows, cols, candidates, group_ns, scan_ns, leaf_ns.

items.title: ModelTree.quantile
items.text:
pythonquantile((self, /, x, tau)) Conditional quantile prediction from the leaves' t-digests: any tau in [0, 1] after the fit. Task: regression.

Args: x: rows of predictors (NA never blocks). tau: quantile level.

Returns: one quantile per row (NaN when a leaf's digest was dropped).

items.title: ModelTree.split_paths
items.text:
pythonsplit_paths((self, /)) Split columns along each root-to-leaf path. Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: one list of column names per root-to-leaf path (the split columns on that path) — the introspection behind interaction-group checking.

items.title: ModelTree.splits
items.text:
pythonsplits((self, /)) Learned splits. Task: regression.

Args: none.

Returns: one dict per split with col, threshold, missing_left, gain (goodness of split).

items.title: ModelTree.to_dot
items.text: pythonto_dot((self, /)) Graphviz DOT for the tree (render with pygraphviz/graphviz — layout is graphviz's job): pgv.AGraph(string=model.to_dot()).draw("tree.svg", prog="dot").

items.title: ModelTree.training_log
items.text:
pythontraining_log((self, /)) The training log (populated when verbose > 0): scan config, per depth/per node candidate counts, precision grid, timings.

Args: none.

Returns: log lines.
